grid.statement: NLGEOM,Key 'includes large-deflection effects in a static or full transient analysis'; Key=OFF ignores large-deflection effects (a small-deflection analysis is specified) and Key=ON includes large-deflection (large rotation) effects or large strain effects, according to the element type
Command default: large-deflection effects are ignored (NLGEOM,OFF is the default)
When large-deflection effects are included (NLGEOM,ON), stress stiffening effects are also included automatically
If used during the solution (/SOLU), the command is valid only within the first load step; it is also valid in PREP7

dFacts.statement: The command is written NLGEOM,Key and is documented to 'Include large-deflection effects in a static or full transient analysis.'
dFacts.note: Cited line 51992 verified ('NLGEOM,Key' / line 51993 'Includes large-deflection effects in a static or full transient analysis.') but claim is exactly G1.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM is categorized under the SOLUTION solution area as 'Nonlinear Options'.
dFacts.note: Line 51994: 'SOLUTION (p.38):Nonlinear Options (p.40)'. Exact.

dFacts.statement: The Key argument is described as the 'Large-deflection key'.
dFacts.note: Lines 51996-51997: 'Key' / 'Large-deflection key:'. Exact.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,OFF 'Ignores large-deflection effects (that is, a small-deflection analysis is specified)' and this option is the default.
dFacts.note: Cited lines 52004-52005 verified ('Ignores large-deflection effects ... This option is the default.') but the claim is the union of G1 (OFF clause) + G2 (default); adds no new content.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON 'Includes large-deflection (large rotation) effects or large strain effects, according to the element type.'
dFacts.note: Cited lines 52007-52008 verified verbatim, but claim is the ON clause of G1.

dFacts.statement: The command default is that 'Large-deflection effects are ignored'.
dFacts.note: Lines 52009-52010 verified ('Command Default' / 'Large-deflection effects are ignored.') but claim is exactly G2.

dFacts.statement: Large-deflection effects are categorized as either large deflection (or large rotation) or large strain, depending on the element type.
dFacts.note: Lines 52012-52013 verified verbatim (Notes), but semantically restates the ON clause of G1 (effects categorized large deflection/rotation or large strain per element type).

dFacts.statement: When large-deflection effects are included (NLGEOM,ON), stress stiffening effects are also included automatically.
dFacts.note: Line 52015 verified verbatim, but claim is word-for-word G3.

dFacts.statement: If used during the solution (/SOLU), the NLGEOM command is valid only within the first load step.
dFacts.note: Line 52016 verified verbatim, but claim is the first clause of G4 (verbatim).

dFacts.statement: In a large-deflection analysis, pressure loads behave differently than other load types.
dFacts.note: Lines 52017-52018 verified ('pressure loads behave differently than other load types... Load Direction in a Large-Deflection Analysis').

dFacts.statement: The gyroscopic matrix (that occurs due to rotational angular velocity) does not support large-deflection effects; its formulation supports small deflection only.
dFacts.note: Lines 52019-52021 verified verbatim (gyroscopic matrix, small deflection/linear formulation only).

dFacts.statement: When large-deflection effects are included in a substructure or CMS transient analysis use pass, the OUTRES command ignores DSUBres = ALL.
dFacts.note: Lines 52022-52023 verified verbatim.

dFacts.statement: The NLGEOM command is also valid in the PREP7 preprocessing phase.
dFacts.note: Line 52024 verified ('This command is also valid in PREP7.') but claim is the second clause of G4.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM is accessible from the GUI via Main Menu>Preprocessor>Loads>Analysis Type>Analysis Options.
dFacts.note: Line 52026 verified verbatim (Menu Paths).

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM is accessible from the GUI via Main Menu>Solution>Analysis Type>Analysis Options and Solution>Sol'n Controls>Basic.
dFacts.note: Lines 52028-52029 verified verbatim ('Main Menu>Solution>Analysis Type>Analysis Options' / '...Sol'n Controls>Basic').

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON is the APDL switch that enables large-deflection/large-strain (nonlinear geometry) behavior, recomputing element stiffness from the deformed configuration including geometric stiffness effects (SSAT/KG).
dFacts.note: Line 11 (Overview) states exactly this (stiffness recomputed from deformed configuration, geometric stiffness SSAT/KG).

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON is the alias form NLGEOM,1 in APDL and the two are used interchangeably.
dFacts.note: Cited line 11 gives only the alias ('NLGEOM,ON (alias NLGEOM,1)'); the 'used interchangeably' clause is supported at line 36 ('both occur in the sources and are used interchangeably').

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON is required wherever rotations, slenderness effects, buckling margins or large strain matter.
dFacts.note: Line 11: 'so it is required wherever rotations, slenderness effects, buckling margins or large strain matter'. Exact.

dFacts.statement: Verified spellings of the command are NLGEOM,ON, nlgeom,on and alias NLGEOM,1, seen across sample_usr.dat, threaded_connection.dat, extrusion.dat, wirecrimp.dat, springcoil.dat, stent.dat, buckling.dat, cylinderflat.dat, Hot_Rolling_Model.dat and SequentialEmbankmentCase1/Case2.dat.
dFacts.note: Line 35 (Notes, 'Commands verified') lists exactly these spellings and all ten .dat files.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON is turned on in the verified tutorials for every large-deformation case under static, transient, soil (ANTYPE,SOIL) and forming analyses, alongside large-strain material models and contact.
dFacts.note: Line 11: 'turned on for every large-deformation case reviewed, under static, transient, soil (ANTYPE,SOIL) and forming analyses, and it accompanies large-strain material models ... and contact'.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM is used with the buckling example (td-21) for buckling and post-buckling of a ring-stiffened cylinder, with nlgeom,on annotated 'Large deflection is activated'.
dFacts.note: Line 21 (td-21 bullet) verified verbatim.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON is used with the hot-rolling example (td-27) for 3D rezoning, annotated 'Turn on nonlinear geometry effects'.
dFacts.note: Line 23 (td-27 bullet) verified verbatim.

dFacts.statement: NLGEOM,ON is used with the sequential embankment (soil) example (td-52) under ANTYPE,SOIL/geostatic, annotated 'LARGE DEFORMATION TURNED ON'.
dFacts.note: Line 24 (td-52 bullet) verified verbatim (ANTYPE,SOIL, geostatic; Case1/Case2).

dFacts.statement: The buckling Load-control example script issues NLGEOM,1 within the /SOL (SOLUTION) phase before NSUBST and AUTOTS.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 46 = 'NLGEOM,1', preceded by '/SOL' (line 45) and followed by 'NSUBST,10000,0,0' (line 47) and 'AUTOTS,1' (line 48).

dFacts.statement: A Technology Showcase example script issues 'NLGEOM, ON   ! Activate large deflection' in the SOLUTION phase after NROPT,UNSYM for a static solve.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 3374 = 'NLGEOM, ON                ! Activate large deflection', inside the 'Static Solution' block (ANTYPE,STATIC line 3370, NROPT,UNSYM line 3372).

dFacts.statement: The Basic Analysis Guide shows NLGEOM,ON in an example structural transient input listing (ANTYPE,TRANS; TRNOPT,FULL; NLGEOM,ON).
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: lines 853-855 = 'ANTYPE,TRANS' / 'TRNOPT,FULL' / 'NLGEOM,ON' under 'An example input listing for a structural transient analysis' (line 851).

dFacts.statement: The Basic Analysis Guide notes that in a large-deformation analysis (NLGEOM,ON) the element coordinate system is first rotated by the computed rotations.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 7861 = 'In a large-deformation analysis (NLGEOM,ON), the element coordinate system is first rotated by the' + line 7862 'amount of rigid body rotation of the element'. 'Computed rotations' paraphrases 'rigid body rotation'.

dFacts.statement: The Basic Analysis Guide notes that when large rotations (NLGEOM,ON) are used, a static analysis with inertia relief is not exactly valid.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 2656 = 'In the case of large rotations (NLGEOM,ON), a static analysis with inertia relief is not exactly' + 'equivalent to a free body linear transient analysis'. 'Not exactly valid' is a loose paraphrase of 'not exactly equivalent'; caveat supported.

dFacts.statement: The Advanced Analysis Guide requires 'Static analysis with geometric nonlinearity (NLGEOM,ON)' for the 2D-to-3D analysis support.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 528 = 'Static analysis with geometric nonlinearity (NLGEOM,ON).' under '2D-to-3D Analysis > Requirements' table.

dFacts.statement: For element birth and death, unless large-deformation effects are activated (NLGEOM,ON), some element types are reactivated in their originally specified geometric configuration.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: lines 7087-7088 verbatim ('Unless large-deformation effects are activated (NLGEOM,ON), some element types will be reactivated in their originally specified geometric configuration.').

dFacts.statement: For a structural analysis employing element birth and death, the guide instructs to activate large-deflection effects (NLGEOM,ON) in the first load step.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 7149 = 'For a structural analysis, activate large-deflection effects (NLGEOM,ON).' under section 8.4.2.1 'Define the First Load Step'.

dFacts.statement: The Advanced Analysis Guide sample first-load-step input includes 'NLGEOM,ON  ! Turns large-deflection effects on' followed by NROPT,FULL.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 7175 = 'NLGEOM,ON          ! Turns large-deflection effects on' in section 8.4.2.1.1 'Sample Input for First Load Step', followed by 'NROPT,FULL' (line 7176).

dFacts.statement: A transient analysis example in the Advanced Analysis Guide uses geometric nonlinearity activated via NLGEOM,ON.
dFacts.note: grep-confirmed: line 4291 = 'transient analysis (NLGEOM,ON).' (lines 4288-4291: rotating-structure inertia effects 'automatically included in a nonlinear transient analysis (NLGEOM,ON)'). Chapter 5 intro prose, not a script block; 'example' is loose but the core claim (transient analysis with geometric nonlinearity via NLGEOM,ON) is supported at the cited line.
